clue.text: Notoriously surreptitious tirade by convict on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside says the convict and tirade are placed within the surreptitious word

parts.note: fly is an informal word for sly or artful

indicators.note: by means next to, so the tirade sits alongside the convict

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict, an old lag
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A convict secretly rants from within prison walls, notoriously so.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly is British slang for knowing or artful, which stretches to surreptitious; 'by' just sets the tirade beside the convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done flagrantly is done openly and scandalously, which is what notoriously conveys.

clue.text: Pretentious uniform United hire out around November

parts.note: flat means even or uniform, as in a flat rate
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

indicators.note: around says the hire-out word wraps round the November letter

parts.note: to let is to hire out property
N is November in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A football club's kit is being hired out, with something happening around November.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulent figuratively means pompous or inflated in style, full of hot air, hence pretentious.

clue.text: Allure cheers up area

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: An area's charm makes everyone cheer up.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you, equivalent to cheers.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to tempt or draw in, the same as attract; both are verbs here.

clue.text: English couple backtracking after a company order

indicators.note: after places the English and couple pieces behind the a and company pieces
backtracking means the couple word is read in reverse

parts.note: an item is a couple in a relationship

explanation.surface: An English couple retrace their steps after placing a company order.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a religious order: the Acoemeti were an early order of monks who kept continuous prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acoemeti were a fifth-century monastic community known as the sleepless ones, a religious order.

clue.text: Hope to stop at this one theft, hoarded for distribution

indicators.note: for distribution suggests the letters being shared out and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief hopes this hoarded haul is the last one before sharing it out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the final point of a journey or effort, where one would hope to finish and stop.

clue.text: Solvers bagging second in arts degree in a foreign language

indicators.note: bagging means the solvers word holds the picked letter inside

parts.note: the setter addresses solvers as you

indicators.note: second in picks the second letter of arts

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: Solvers taking an arts degree study a foreign language.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoruba is a language of south-western Nigeria and Benin, spoken by the Yoruba people.

clue.text: Vagrant starts to head off before others

indicators.note: starts to means take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A wanderer sets off ahead of everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a homeless wandering person, a tramp, so a vagrant.

clue.text: Handle left on extremely lofty north Lakeland peak

parts.note: a helve is the handle of an axe or tool

indicators.note: extremely means take only the extreme letters, first and last, of lofty

explanation.surface: A walking guide describes a handle-shaped route on the left of a lofty northern Lakeland mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Lakeland is the English Lake District in Cumbria.
explanation.definitionFit: Helvellyn is one of the highest mountains in the English Lake District, a well-known fell.

clue.text: Old president overseeing pledge of intended code of chivalry

indicators.note: overseeing in a down clue means the president sits above the pledge

parts.note: Bush was a former US president, either George Bush
I do is the vow said by a bride or groom at a wedding

explanation.surface: A former president supervises a fiance's pledge to follow a code of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai's traditional Japanese code of honour, loyalty and martial conduct.

clue.text: Heartless fool stopping 23 about cure

indicators.note: stopping means the trimmed fool plugs the gap inside the reversed volcano
about means the volcano's name is turned round

parts.note: the answer to 23 across, the volcano

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the fool word is removed

parts.note: an idiot is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone foolish blocking a volcano's eruption hopes for a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts poison, so a cure.

clue.text: Enjoy something saucy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take pleasure in
second meaning: a sauce or pickle served as a condiment

explanation.walkthrough: Saucy looks like it means cheeky or risque, but here it is literal: a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for savouring with pleasure and a noun for a tangy pickle or chutney.

clue.text: State of symmetric pair of Autobahn sections

indicators.note: symmetric pair of says to keep two letter pairs placed mirror-wise in the word
sections means parts cut from the word, the mirrored two-letter stretches either side of its centre

explanation.surface: A traveller describes the condition of some stretches of German motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: In AUTOBAHN, the second and third letters (UT) mirror the sixth and seventh (AH); keeping those two pairs and discarding the rest leaves the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Mountain West.

clue.text: Matt O'Brien trained flowering plant

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters being shaped or directed like a climbing plant into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener named Matt O'Brien trained a flowering plant along a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Montbretia is a garden perennial of the iris family with orange flowers, also called crocosmia.

clue.text: Blackmail divorcee, perhaps twisting, getting caught

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse, a divorcee for example

indicators.note: getting caught means heard, so the twisting word is taken by its sound

parts.note: torsion is the act of twisting

explanation.surface: A divorcee resorts to blackmail, twisting the facts until caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: Caught here means heard: TORSION, said aloud, gives TORTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion is obtaining money by threats or force, of which blackmail is the classic form.

clue.text: Agreed over leg measurement in turn up

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: in places the leg and measurement pieces inside the turn-up word

parts.note: to turn up something is to find it
on is the leg side in cricket
an em is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A tailor agrees on an inside-leg measurement for a trouser turn-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side of a cricket field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: People of one mind are in agreement, so the phrase means agreed as an adjective.

clue.text: Defeat following no-score draw between sides

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: between puts the two noughts inside the pair of side letters

parts.note: left and right are the two sides, L and R
a nil-nil draw is written as two noughts

explanation.surface: A team suffers defeat after a goalless draw.
explanation.walkthrough: A no-score draw in football is 0-0, giving two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to knock them down or beat them, so to defeat.

clue.text: Animals spared and set free

indicators.note: set free means the letters are released and rearranged

explanation.surface: Some animals were spared and released into the wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Red pandas are small reddish tree-dwelling mammals of the Himalayas, so animals.

clue.text: Trucker loading tonnes into ship after moving cover

indicators.note: loading means the tonnes letter is put inside
after moving cover means the letter covering the front of the ship word is shifted along

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship
T is the abbreviation for tonnes

explanation.surface: A trucker loads tonnes of cargo into a ship after moving its covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift the S from the front of STEAMER to give TEAMSER, then load T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Teamster is the American word for a lorry driver, originally a driver of a team of horses.

clue.text: Finish off project number one for Bronski Beat

indicators.note: finish off says the final letter of the project word is removed
for means the picked letter stands in place of the removed one

parts.note: to throw is to project

indicators.note: number one picks the first letter of Bronski

explanation.surface: A pop fan's top project concerns the synth band Bronski Beat.
explanation.walkthrough: Bronski Beat were a 1980s British synth-pop band; Beat looks part of their name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a pulsing rhythm, a beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Lock-keeper from Tehran travelling around India

indicators.note: around says the reworked city wraps round the India letter
travelling means the letters of Tehran move about into a new order

parts.note: I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone travels from Tehran around India, perhaps a canal lock-keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock-keeper looks like a canal worker; the locks are of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet keeps locks of hair in place, so it is a witty keeper of locks.

clue.text: Dog, rushed into duties, recalled across river

indicators.note: across means the reversed combination stretches over the river letter, holding it inside
recalled means the combination is called back, so read in reverse
into says the rushed word goes inside the duties word

parts.note: debts are duties, things owed
ran means rushed

explanation.surface: A dog rushed into its tasks and was called back from across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: DEBTS holding RAN gives DRANEBTS; 'recalled' turns it to STBENARD, which then spans R.
explanation.definitionFit: The St Bernard is a large Alpine breed famed for mountain rescue, a kind of dog.

clue.text: Reassert case over including player

indicators.note: over in a down clue means those contained letters are read upwards
including says the letters are contained within the clue words

explanation.surface: Someone restates a case, covering a player too.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Reassert case' backwards to find the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is a performer on stage, and an actress is a female performer.

clue.text: Oriental art work ultimately attracting deep breath perhaps when removed from case

indicators.note: attracting means the work letter draws the trimmed breath to it
ultimately picks the last letter of work
removed from case means the outer letters of the breath word are taken off

parts.note: a lungful is a deep breath, for example

explanation.surface: Doing oriental martial art involves taking a deep breath after removing something from its case.
explanation.definitionFit: Kung fu is a Chinese martial art, and martial arts from East Asia are oriental arts.

clue.text: Cheap show by awful medium entertaining me, later us

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of medium are badly jumbled
entertaining means the jumbled medium takes in the me piece among its letters
later means us is also taken in, further along than me

explanation.surface: A dreadful medium performs a cheap show, first for me and then for the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's picture is two separate guests placed apart inside the jumbled medium; the app pools all three as one jumble, which spells the same letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime museum was a cheap American popular exhibition of curiosities in the nineteenth century, so a cheap show.

clue.text: Regularly observed Neptunian mountain

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of Neptunian

explanation.surface: A mountain is seen on a regular basis on Neptune.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, a mountain.

clue.text: Finish, as do Gog and Magog

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a conclusion or end

explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are legendary giants, but the clue cares only about their final letter: they both end in G.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the close or conclusion of something, a finish.

clue.text: Where to find third man to duel if ill

indicators.note: ill means badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sick man challenged to a duel wonders where to find a third party.
explanation.walkthrough: Third man is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the off side, out near the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Third man is a fielding position in cricket deep on the field, in the outfield region.

clue.text: Boss of film company refusing one Oscar

indicators.note: refusing means the studio word does without those letters

parts.note: a studio is a film company

O is Oscar in the NATO alphabet

clue.text: Subordinate settles in courtroom clothes

parts.note: under means lower in rank, subordinate
